answer: Unique-egress throttling stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent registers one provider-verified egress IP range, so one network holds few. Second, jobs per egress are capped weekly, so a farm behind one address earns little. Third, peers audit logs monthly, and shared ranges trigger review. Fourth, fraud burns a $25 bond and blocks it a year. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 egresses at $8 monthly plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is an island against the tide, a mirror proving each agent stands alone, like one stallholder barred from a hundred stalls at one door.
